incidents.name: MulticallWithXera
incidents.notes: Xera token's _msgSender() trusted the Multicall forwarder, so aggregate3 transferFrom spoofed the victim as sender and spent its approval to Multicall.

sources.ref: Onchain review: victim 0x90be00229fe8000000009e007743a485d400c3b7 created 2025-06-11T06:24:53Z (BSC block 51252670) by 0x94496c681152c6f44698801620a7c52a14d77506, not the attack-tx sender 0x00b700b9da0053009cb84400ed1e8fe251002af3. keccak(eth_getCode) is identical at the creation and incident blocks, storage slots 0-25 are entirely empty and no EIP-1967/beacon slot is set, and the single DELEGATECALL in the runtime takes its target from calldata (CALLDATALOAD/SHR feeding the address operand), i.e. a per-call forward rather than a stored implementation pointer; the exploit trace contains no DELEGATECALL out of the victim. Deployment basis is exact.
